About Us
At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.
At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.
The Role:
We are seeking a highly skilled AI Security Research & Red team engineer to join our Red Team within the Security Threat Detection, Response and Emulation organization. This is a critical role that will be at the forefront of protecting our company and customers from malicious threats. You will be responsible for driving security research, exercises, and activities that emulate real world attackers and attacks to drive improvements in Cloudflare’s security posture focusing on AI, Agents, harnesses and LLM’s.
Key Responsibilities:
AI Security and Vulnerability Research: Stay current with emerging threats and perform deep-dive research to identify AI-specific vulnerabilities and risks in addition to general vulnerabilities across Cloudflare’s products and services.
Agentic testing and adoption: As a core function, identifying AI-related attack surfaces through rigorous testing of agentic implementations and LLM usage which will help define requirements and implementation guidance while proactively.
Adversary Simulation: Execution of full-chain red team operations targeting Cloudflare’s global infrastructure, corporate networks, and product ecosystems.
Efficacy Testing: Establish a rigorous framework for testing "Security Efficacy"—measuring exactly how well our WAF, EDR, and SIEM detections perform against known TTPs (Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures).
Purple Teaming: Foster a highly collaborative relationship with the Blue Team (Detection & Response) to ensure findings are translated into immediate defensive improvements.
Mentorship & Growth: Be a technical leader, providing technical expertise while fostering a culture of curiosity, ethical hacking and partnering to improve Cloudflare’s security posture.
Executive Reporting: Translate complex technical exploits into risk-based narratives for leadership, helping prioritize engineering resources where they matter most.
Partnerships
Security Incident Response Team (SIRT): You will act as the "sparring partner" for SIRT. By conducting unannounced exercises, you help them refine their playbooks, test their on-call rotations, and ensure their forensic tooling is effective under pressure.
Threat Detection & Threat Engineering: You will partner closely with these teams to bridge the gap between adversary simulation and defensive coverage. You will proactively identify detection gaps, lead the development of new detection logic, and establish rigorous validation frameworks to test and tune detections against emerging TTPs.
Product Engineering/SRE: We operate as "Customer Zero" of our own products, your red teaming findings will drive resilience in processes and implementations, ultimately making Cloudflare and its customers more secure.
Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC): You will bridge the gap between "paper security" and "technical reality." By providing empirical evidence of control effectiveness, you help GRC move away from manual audits and toward continuous, automated compliance validation.
Required Qualifications:
Experience: 4+ years in offensive security, application security or other relevant field
Deep knowledge: AI, Coding agents, LLMs, prompt engineering, AI-related attack vectors (e.g., prompt injection, jailbreaking), and Agentic concepts all for use in the red team but also testing Cloudflare uses.
Technical Roots: A strong background in manual penetration testing, exploit development, or cloud security (AWS/GCP/Bare Metal).
Operational Mindset: Experience using the MITRE ATT&CK framework to map coverage and identify "blind spots" in defensive telemetry.
Communication Skills: The ability to explain a complex "0-day" exploit to a non-technical stakeholder while maintaining the respect of a deep-dive engineering team.
Tooling Familiarity: Knowledge of automated breach and attack simulation (BAS) tools, as well as custom-built frameworks for payload delivery and C2 infrastructure.
Compensation
Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location.
For New York based hires: Estimated annual salary of $166,000 - $208,000.
Equity
This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan.
What Makes Cloudflare Special?
We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.
Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.
Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.
1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.
Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

Please note that any offer of employment may be conditioned on your authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export laws without sponsorship for an export license.

About the team
The Finance team is a critical pillar of Cloudflare’s success, translating strategy into financial outcomes, and serving as a trusted voice to the public markets, the Board, and our shareholders. The Investor Relations team is a small, high-impact group that tells Cloudflare’s financial story to the public markets — translating one of the most differentiated technology platforms in the world into a clear, credible, and compelling investment narrative.
About the role
Cloudflare is looking for an Associate, Investor Relations & Strategic Finance to join our lean IR team and help power how we engage with Wall Street. You will be a core contributor to the quarterly earnings cycle, our consensus and financial modeling work, investor events including our annual Investor Day, and strategic finance projects for senior leadership.
This is a hands-on, high-visibility role. The work you produce will go directly to the CFO, CEO, Board, and public markets, so we hold ourselves to an exceptionally high bar on accuracy. You will work closely with Finance, Accounting, Legal, Communications, FP&A, and the executive team, and you will get broad exposure to the business and to the public markets. We are AI-native in how we work, and we expect you to treat modern tooling as a force multiplier on insight, productivity, and rigor.
What you’ll do
Quarterly earnings and consensus
Support the end-to-end quarterly earnings process, helping draft and assemble the press release, supplemental financial information, prepared remarks, Q&A prep, and investor deck.
Build and maintain our consensus model: collect and analyze sell-side estimates and models, and benchmark them against internal forecasts.
Support the guidance process, including share count forecasting, sensitivity analyses, and supporting materials for leadership.
Drive tie-out and validation work so that every figure, claim, and disclosure across the press release, supplemental, scripts, Q&A, deck, 10-Q, and 10-K is accurate and consistent.
Help prepare for earnings Q&A: anticipated questions, peer transcript research, key stats and proof points, and live-call backup material.
Coordinate the post-earnings analyst callback program, including scheduling, notes, and feedback summaries.
Investor engagement
Support day-to-day engagement with sell-side analysts and institutional investors, including responding to inbound requests and maintaining our investor database.
Help plan and run investor events, including sell-side conferences, one-on-ones, on-site investor visits, and non-deal roadshows.
Prepare briefing materials for the CEO, CFO, and other executives ahead of investor meetings, including investor profiles, talking points, and Q&A prep.
Maintain core IR collateral, including the investor presentation, fact sheets, and IR website content.
Analyze shareholder ownership and support investor targeting.
Investor Day and strategic finance projects
Support the planning and execution of our annual Investor Day, including the invite tracker and registration, content drafting, validation, and day-of logistics.
Contribute to strategic finance projects such as peer benchmarking, competitive analyses, long-range financial modeling, and ad-hoc analyses for senior leadership.
Analytics and tooling
Monitor and synthesize analyst coverage, peer results, investor sentiment, and industry trends into clear, actionable summaries for leadership.
Build and maintain the models, dashboards, trackers, and validation tools that let a small team operate at scale.
Use AI-native tooling and automation to improve speed, accuracy, and insight across the IR function.
Examples of desirable skills, knowledge and experience
3–5 years of experience in investment banking, equity research, investor relations, FP&A, corporate finance, or equity investing; exposure to public technology companies is a plus.
Strong financial modeling skills , including building and maintaining operating models, consensus models, and share count and dilution forecasts.
Solid understanding of financial statements , public-company reporting, and valuation; familiarity with SaaS or consumption-based revenue models is a plus.
Strong written communication skills , with the ability to draft clear, concise materials for senior executives and to turn complex financial or technical concepts into simple narratives.
Exceptional attention to detail , and pride in getting every number right.
An ownership mindset : you are organized, take initiative, and can manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment, especially during earnings season.
High-trust collaboration , with the ability to work effectively with teams across Finance, Accounting, Legal, and Communications.
AI-native curiosity and skill : fluency with modern AI tooling and a track record of using it to amplify your impact.
Sound judgment with confidential information , including awareness of materiality, fair disclosure, and Reg FD (or a strong willingness to learn).
Genuine interest in cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure, developer platforms, or AI, and in the public markets.
Compensation
Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location.
For Bay Area based hires: Estimated annual salary of $117,000 - $161,000

Available Locations
San Francisco, US
We are only considering locally based candidates OR candidates looking to move to the Bay Area.
Customer Engineer - (AI & Start-Ups)
About the Role
Digital Native SEs at Cloudflare work with the most innovative and cutting-edge companies on the planet — the startups and high-growth, cloud-native businesses that are building the next generation of Internet products. These are companies where the developers are the decision makers, and where the CTO is often personally responsible for shipping new products and getting the company's AI initiatives off the ground.
This role is for a technologist who genuinely enjoys being in the room with builders. You'll be equally comfortable jumping into a Slack channel with a founding engineer, whiteboarding an architecture with a lead developer, and stepping into a strategic conversation with a CTO about their platform and AI roadmap. You speak the language of engineers fluently and can hold a credible, detailed technical conversation — but this is not a software developer role, and you won't be writing production code every day. Your superpower is technical discovery, translation, and evangelism: understanding what a builder is trying to accomplish, mapping it to the full breadth of the Cloudflare Developer Platform, and inspiring teams to build on Cloudflare rather than just consume a single service.
The Digital Native segment leans heavily on Solutions Engineering to lead technical discovery within the cloud-developer vertical. You'll be expected to go deep on the Cloudflare Developer Platform — Workers, Durable Objects, Workers AI, R2, KV, D1, Vectorize, Queues, Pages, and the broader developer ecosystem — far beyond basic storage, and to make the case for Cloudflare as the place to build. This role covers both the acquisition of new Digital Native accounts and the expansion of existing ones. The ideal candidate is a "builder" personality with a strong mix of pre-sales/technical customer-facing experience who thrives in an agile, fast-moving environment.
What you'll do as a Senior Solutions Engineer
The Pre-Sales Solution Engineering organization owns the technical sales of the Cloudflare solution portfolio, ensuring maximal business value, fit-for-purpose solution design and adoption roadmap for our customers. Solution Engineering is made up of individuals from a wide range of backgrounds including but not limited to Sales Consultants, Technical Consultants, Technical Support and Program Managers.
You are a customer-facing technologist within the Cloudflare Solutions Engineering team, focused on the developer-first, digital-native segment. You have experience in a pre-sales or other technical customer-facing role, and you're at your best when engaging directly with engineering teams and technical founders. In this role you'll partner closely with the sales team from the very start of the cycle — joining early discovery calls, qualifying opportunities from the get-go, and embedding yourself in customer Slack channels and working sessions. You'll lead technical discovery, deliver compelling demos and architecture discussions, run proof-of-concept builds, and evangelize the Cloudflare Developer Platform as the foundation for our customers' next products and AI initiatives.
Responsibilities
Specifically, we are looking for you to:
Lead technical discovery within the cloud-developer vertical — asking the right questions to uncover how a customer builds, what they're trying to ship, and where Cloudflare fits.
Engage early and often: join sales-led discovery calls from the outset, help qualify deals from the get-go, and stay embedded with customer teams (including in their Slack channels and working sessions) throughout the cycle.
Identify and map customer initiatives and business problems — especially around new product development and AI initiatives — to the Cloudflare platform.
Build relationships and technical champions within customer accounts, from founding engineers and developers up to the CTO.
Develop and present tailored technical content and demos for both hands-on developer audiences and senior technical leadership.
Lead demo and proof-of-concept / build activities for Cloudflare prospects and customers.
Evangelize the Cloudflare Developer Platform (Workers, Workers AI, Durable Objects, R2, D1, KV, Vectorize, Queues, Pages and more) — making the case for customers to build on Cloudflare, not just use it for storage or CDN.
Demonstrate your expertise with your peers through the creation of professional content, including reference architectures, demos, blog posts and other knowledge-sharing activities.
Represent and evangelize Cloudflare externally at Developer, Community, Technology and Industry events with thought leadership and expertise.
Apply in-depth vertical knowledge or domain expertise. Advise on best practices.
Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience
Previous experience as a Solutions Engineer or other customer-facing technical role, ideally selling to or working with developer-led, cloud-native, or startup organizations.
A genuine "builder" mindset and the personality to match: you enjoy talking to developers, you're curious, and you naturally gravitate toward technical problem-solving conversations.
The ability to speak engineers' language credibly — you can hold your own on architecture, APIs, and platform design — without this being a hands-on, code-every-day developer role.
Strong technical discovery instincts: you know how to draw out requirements, qualify fit early, and separate real needs from noise.
A good mix of pre-sales / technical sales experience and comfort operating in an agile, fast-moving environment (joining Slack channels, iterating quickly, engaging in early-stage calls, and qualifying deals from the start).
Solid communication, written and presentation skills, with the range to talk to both a hands-on developer and a CTO in the same day.
Ability to work on several projects and activities concurrently.
Highly driven, curious, team-oriented, and able to work with a sense of urgency.
You've built web applications before, or contributed to existing web applications in a meaningful way — enough to have real empathy for how developers work.
Polished communication and executive presentation skills with the ability to drive a discussion with a broad range of stakeholders (from the web developer to the CTO/CISO).
Relationship building: a proven track record of building deep technical relationships with engineers and technical founders. Experience managing various stakeholder relationships to build consensus on technical solutions/projects.
Experience managing technical sales within accounts, including developing champion-style relationships, driving technical wins, and assisting with technical validation.
Bachelor's Degree or equivalent in relevant work experience.
The role requires up to 50% travel to attend meetings with prospects or customers, attend conferences and other industry events, and to collaborate with your Cloudflare teammates.
A deep understanding of the Cloudflare Developer Platform and core industry components (and a desire to learn more):
The Cloudflare Developer Platform — serverless compute and application development with Workers, Durable Objects, Workers AI, R2, KV, D1, Vectorize, Queues, and Pages. Familiarity with building or architecting applications on a serverless/edge platform is a strong plus.
AI/GenAI application patterns — inference at the edge, RAG, vector databases, and how startups are operationalizing AI initiatives.
HTTP technologies including reverse proxy (e.g., WAF and CDN), forward proxy (secure web gateway), and serverless application development.
Internet security technologies including DDoS and DDoS mitigation, Firewalls, TLS, VPN, DLP.
Networking technologies including TCP, UDP, DNS, IPv4 + IPv6, BGP routing, GRE, SD-WAN, MPLS, Global Traffic Management.
Zero-trust network access (ZTNA & SASE) concepts including identity management and authentication.
Cloud computing technologies such as AWS, GCP, Azure and others.
Some scripting or programming familiarity with one or more of JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Golang, BASH — enough to read code, build a demo, and converse with engineers (not to ship production software).
Understanding of, or experience with, regulatory requirements such as FedRAMP, GDPR, PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOC-2, ISO/IEC.

Proactively monitor customer health scores and telemetry to ensure rapid time-to-value, resolve integration bottlenecks, and reduce deployment risk.

Trusted Advisory: Act as a trusted technical advisor throughout the entire customer lifecycle, maintaining a continuous, deep relationship with key stakeholders from initial onboarding through maturity, renewal, and expansion. Provide thought partnership on architecture, AI control layers, security posture, and deployment confidence. Identify potential deployment risks or integration bottlenecks early, and provide remediation strategies to de-risk customer outcomes.

Education & Enablement: Partner closely with the Enablement Team to design, build, and govern technical resources. Architectural Mindset: Ability to white-board, design, and articulate complex enterprise network and security architectures clearly.
Consultative & Advisory Skills: Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate deeply technical concepts into business outcomes for both hands-on engineers and C-level executives.

Security: Expertise in the security of Internet properties, including WAF, Bot Management, Firewalls, Rate Limiting, (M)TLS, Zero Trust, and SASE concepts.

Cloudflare is looking for an Automation Specialist to transform how our global Data Center Security Compliance (DCSC) team operates. This critical role is part of the Infrastructure Operations organization, which is responsible for building, scaling, and running Cloudflare's data center and network infrastructure across 700+ sites worldwide.
The DCSC team manages physical access control and compliance auditing across one of the most complex and distributed infrastructure footprints in the industry, spanning more than 105 vendor portals, hundreds of non-portal carrier-neutral and edge partner sites, and multiple regulatory frameworks including SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, ISMAP, and IRAP. The operational burden of this work is substantial and largely manual: user lists are pulled by hand, access control lists are reconciled by eye, evidence packages are assembled ticket by ticket, and attestation cycles consume weeks of coordinator time every quarter.
This role exists to change that. The DCSC Automation -Specialist will design, build, and operate AI-assisted and automated workflows that eliminate the most time-consuming manual work in the DCSC operating model, freeing compliance coordinators to focus on exception handling, stakeholder relationships, and regulatory judgment rather than data gathering and reconciliation.
This is a builder role. You will interview the team to understand each workflow, identify the highest-leverage automation targets, and ship tooling that demonstrably reduces the time it takes to close a QAR cycle, produce an audit evidence package, or manage a batch of access provisioning requests. You will work in close partnership with the DCSC coordinators, and existing automation developers, and will own the DCSC operational tooling roadmap.
Key Responsibilities
Portal Automation & User List Extraction
Browser Automation: Design and maintain automated scripts (Playwright, Puppeteer, or equivalent) that log into vendor data center portals, extract user access lists, and feed structured output into the DCSC Portal and comparison pipelines replacing manual portal-by-portal data collection across 105+ portals covering 338+ sites.
Resilience & Coverage: Build fallback handling for portals that block or rate-limit automated access; document exceptions and maintain a coverage registry tracking automation status per portal.
Scheduled Execution: Operationalize extraction jobs on a recurring cadence aligned to QAR and MAR cycles, with alerting for failures and drift.
ACL Reconciliation & Diff Engine
Automated Comparison: Build tooling that ingests portal-extracted user lists and compares them against the master Access Control List (ACL), automatically surfacing discrepancies: users present in a portal but absent from the ACL, users on the ACL without active portal access, and role or access-level mismatches.
Exception-Only Output: Route confirmed discrepancies directly to pre-populated Jira tickets for human review and action, eliminating the need for coordinators to perform full manual review of every user record each quarter.
Audit Trail: Ensure all comparison runs produce immutable, timestamped records suitable for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and FedRAMP evidence requirements.
Attestation & Evidence Automation
Attestation Module: Own and extend the attestation workflow within the DCSC Portal, including automated cycle triggering, manager notification, time-stamped confirmation capture, and exception escalation, replacing manual screenshot-based evidence gathering.
Evidence Package Builder: Build automated pipelines that compile audit-ready evidence packages for SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, ISMAP, and IRAP control cycles, pulling attestation logs, portal extraction results, diff reports, and correspondence into structured packages keyed to specific control IDs.
GRC Alignment: Work directly with GRC counterparts to validate that automated evidence formats meet auditor and regulatory requirements before deployment.
AI-Assisted Anomaly Detection & Triage
Access Pattern Analysis: Implement LLM-based review passes over QAR cycle output to surface patterns warranting human escalation: former employees retaining access, access creep over time, dormant accounts, and anomalous role assignments across sites.
Ticket Intelligence: Build automation that reads incoming Jira onboarding and offboarding tickets and generates structured, portal-specific action checklists reducing coordinator cognitive load and preventing missed steps across multi-portal provisioning workflows.
Continuous Improvement: Monitor automation output quality over time, retrain or recalibrate models as portal structures change, and maintain a feedback loop with coordinators on false positives and missed detections.
DCSC Portal Ownership & Tooling Roadmap
Platform Stewardship: Own the DCSC Portal as the operational runtime for all automation and workflow tooling ensuring it remains stable, documented, and usable by coordinators without engineering support for day-to-day tasks.
Roadmap Management: Maintain a prioritized backlog of automation opportunities, assessed by time savings, compliance impact, and implementation complexity; present quarterly progress and priorities to DCSC leadership.
Documentation: Produce runbooks for every automation, ensuring that no operational capability lives only in one person's head or on a local machine.
Desirable skills / Experience:
Automation Engineering: Demonstrated experience building browser automation (Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, or equivalent) against real-world web applications, including handling authentication flows, dynamic content, and anti-bot mitigations.
TypeScript Proficiency: Strong skills for scripting, data wrangling, structured file I/O, and API integration. Ability to write maintainable, documented code that non-engineers can operate.
LLM Integration: Hands-on experience integrating LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or equivalent) into production workflows for classification, drafting, summarization, or anomaly detection tasks.
Data Engineering Fundamentals: Comfort working with structured and semi-structured data at scale, diffing datasets, normalizing inconsistent formats, and producing clean outputs for downstream audit use.
API & Workflow Integration: Experience building integrations with ticketing or ITSM systems (Jira preferred) via REST API, including automated ticket creation, status updates, and attachment handling.
Systems Thinking: Ability to map an end-to-end manual workflow, identify the highest-leverage automation insertion points, and ship incrementally without waiting for a perfect solution.
Workflow Archaeology: Comfortable extracting process knowledge from subject-matter experts through structured interviews turning tribal knowledge into documented, automatable workflows.
Bias Toward Simplicity: Strong product intuition for the minimum viable automation that delivers real time savings, rather than over-engineering for edge cases.
Compliance Awareness: Appreciation for the stakes of accuracy in a compliance context, understanding that an incorrect ACL diff or a missing evidence artifact has real audit consequences.
Soft Skills:
Communication: Able to explain automation design decisions and tradeoffs clearly to non-technical stakeholders including compliance coordinators and GRC partners.
Ambiguity Tolerance: Vendor portals don't come with documentation. Workflows are passed down verbally. You need to be energized by figuring things out from scratch.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with Cloudflare Workers or similar edge compute platforms
Familiarity with GRC/compliance frameworks (SOC 2, FedRAMP, ISO 27001) at an operational level — not as an auditor, but enough to understand why evidence integrity matters
RPA tooling experience (UiPath, Power Automate) as fallback for portals that defeat headless browsers
Prior work in infrastructure operations, data center, or physical security environments
Experience building internal tooling or developer-facing portals (not just scripts)

Deep technical fluency with public-company reporting, financial statements, capital markets, valuation methodologies, and SaaS / consumption-based revenue models. Comfort debating modeling assumptions and valuation mechanics.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills — including the ability to draft in the voice of senior executives, translate complex technical or financial concepts into clear narratives for non-technical audiences, and operate confidently in high-stakes external communications.
Advanced financial modeling skills — fluency in building, maintaining, and stress-testing operating models, share-count and dilution forecasts, guidance sensitivity analyses, and consensus benchmarks.
An ownership mindset — comfort owning a process end-to-end, driving operational structure in a fast-paced environment, and operating with the integrity and accuracy demanded by external disclosure.
High-trust collaboration — the ability to build credibility quickly with senior internal stakeholders (CFO, CEO, Board, Legal, Accounting, FP&A) and external stakeholders (sell-side analysts, institutional investors).
AI-native curiosity and skill — fluency with modern AI tooling and a track record of using it to amplify your impact. We are building an AI-forward organization and the right candidate sees AI as a partner, not a threat.
Sound judgment with confidential information — a clear understanding of materiality, fair disclosure, Reg FD, and the discretion required when working with pre-announcement financial data.

About the Department
Infrastructure Operations builds and manages the data center infrastructure behind Cloudflare's global network. The organization brings together engineering, operations, hardware and logistics teams that plan, deploy, operate and maintain our footprint in hundreds of cities worldwide. In this role, you'll help extend that footprint with a new generation of data center sites across the United States.
About the Role
We're looking for an experienced Data Center Operations manager to build and run the team that brings these new sites online and keeps them running around the clock.
You will build a distributed team of Data Center Engineers from the ground up. You'll own sites across their full lifecycle: delivering greenfield builds through third-party vendors and colocation partners, running them in production, and retiring hardware securely at end of life. You'll be accountable for production hardware availability, 24x7 on-site response, and the operating model that lets this footprint scale.
The role means balancing competing demands every day: build deadlines against build quality, dependence on partners against high standards, and fast incident response against careful compliance. You need to keep both sides of each in view.
This role covers the physical layer: hardware, cabling, and Layer 1/Layer 2 connectivity. It works closely with network engineering and server provisioning teams but does not own them.
What You'll Do
Team Leadership
Hire, develop and manage Data Center Engineers based on-site at data centers across the US. Set clear expectations, career paths and a culture of ownership across a team spread over many sites.
Build and take part in a 24x7 on-call rotation with your team. Define coverage models, handover protocols and incident SLAs that hold up as the footprint grows.
Serve as the escalation point for on-site incidents. Coordinate engineers, colocation providers and vendors to restore service quickly, and lead root-cause analysis after major incidents so the same problem doesn't happen again.
Site Delivery
Own build timelines from site readiness through hardware delivery, rack-and-stack, cabling, validation and handoff to production.
Run greenfield builds as multi-workstream programs. Coordinate third-party integrators, contractors and colocation providers to hit dates without cutting corners.
Be on-site during key build phases to oversee vendor work, verify quality and make sure sites are production-ready.
Production Operations
Be accountable for availability targets for production hardware at your sites. Run break/fix, repairs, RMAs and spares strategy so that availability is measured, reported and improving.
Manage colocation providers and vendors day to day: escalations, remote-hands quality, power and cooling issues, and performance against contractual commitments.
Documentation and DCIM
Make sure every site is fully documented in DCIM from day one. That covers rack elevations, power and cabling, asset location, and lifecycle status, all recorded as hardware arrives rather than filled in later.
Treat infrastructure records as a source of truth that both operations and dependent teams rely on, giving them accurate, current visibility into where hardware is and what state it's in.
Partner with tooling teams to bring DCIM online at new sites, and define documentation standards that hold up as the footprint grows.
Decommissioning and Hardware Lifecycle
Own on-site decommissioning end to end: unracking, physical collections, serial number verification, chain of custody, and handoff for secure destruction.
Partner with vendor management on IT asset disposition (ITAD) vendors. Make sure destruction certificates and compliance evidence are filed and audit-ready.
Security and Compliance
Make sure your sites and team meet Cloudflare's physical security, access control, chain-of-custody and compliance obligations.
Follow established physical access procedures, and work with security and compliance teams to develop new ones where these sites need them.
Support audits with accurate, timely evidence. Treat audit readiness as a continuous standard, not something you prepare for once per audit cycle.
Automation and Operational Efficiency
Find manual, repetitive work in build, break/fix, decommissioning and evidence collection. Influence tooling and automation teams to remove it.
Evaluate and adopt AI-assisted workflows for incident triage, root-cause analysis, documentation and compliance evidence generation.
Scale the operation through tooling, not just headcount.
Business Reporting
Own weekly business reviews and monthly and quarterly reporting on availability, build progress, incidents and operational health to the Director and peer leaders.
Partner with network, systems, hardware, supply chain and infrastructure engineering teams to make sure physical operations support what runs on top of them.
Who You Are
A builder who stays to operate. You've stood up sites and teams, and you take ownership of what happens after go-live. Delivering a build is where your job starts. If it isn't documented, it isn't done.
A leader of distributed teams. You've hired and built trust with on-site engineers spread across many locations, most of whom you won't see day to day. You know how to create accountability, consistent standards and a shared culture across sites, both remotely and in person.
Firm with partners. You hold colocation providers and vendors to high standards without becoming adversarial. You know the contract, you track performance, and you escalate when it's warranted.
Compliance-minded without being a compliance specialist. You understand why access controls and decommissioning chain of custody are audit controls. You treat compliance as part of doing the work well, not as overhead.
Automation-first. When something hurts, your first instinct is to fix the process or the tooling, not add people. You can turn an operational pain point into requirements engineering teams can act on.
Required Experience
6+ years in data center operations, including 3+ years directly managing on-site technical teams. At least part of that time should be leading geographically distributed teams.
A track record of operating multi-site data center fleets at hyperscale or large-cloud scale.
Hands-on experience with IT hardware, including servers, network devices, optics and cabling, not only facilities infrastructure.
Enough hands-on depth to coach engineers on technical work and to judge the quality of vendor and contractor work.
Experience owning sites across the full lifecycle: delivering greenfield data center or cage builds through third-party vendors, running them in steady state, and decommissioning hardware.
Experience managing providers in Tier III+ colocation facilities and holding them accountable to commitments.
Experience managing 24x7 on-call operations and incident escalation.
Strong Layer 1 and Layer 2 fundamentals: structured cabling, fiber and optics, patching standards, switching basics, and troubleshooting physical connectivity for network and server hardware.
Solid knowledge of data center power and cooling, rack design, high-density deployments and hardware lifecycle management.
Strong understanding of DCIM and asset management systems. You should have a track record of keeping documentation accurate from day one, including rack, power, cabling and asset records maintained from hardware arrival through decommissioning.
Working knowledge of the security and compliance frameworks common in enterprise-grade data centers. You should understand them well enough to run operations under them; auditor-level expertise isn't required.
Strong program management skills across multiple vendors, sites and time-bound workstreams.
A track record of reducing toil through tooling or process redesign.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including regular business reviews and status, risk and availability reporting to leadership.
Ability to travel regularly to data center sites. Expect more frequent travel during site builds, shifting to periodic visits as sites reach steady state.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience standing up a new data center operations function or region from zero.
Background at a hyperscaler, cloud provider, major CDN or similarly fast-scaling infrastructure company.
Experience with ITAD vendor programs and secure destruction requirements.
Experience with PagerDuty or similar on-call and incident tooling.
Familiarity with DCIM and source-of-truth tooling such as NetBox or Nlyte, Jira-based operational workflows, and Confluence documentation practices.
Experience with remote-hands programs and vendor scorecards.
Background in hardware diagnostics, burn-in or automated build validation.

Lead and Grow Engineering Talent (Player-Coach Model): Recruit, mentor, and develop a diverse team of talented software and data engineers while leading by example through active code contributions, hands-on technical guidance, and unblocking engineers directly in the codebase.
Architect & Build Platform Primitives: Set the technical vision and actively write code for our GTM Data Platform, App Platform, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations in Go and TypeScript, enabling internal teams to build and scale maintainable solutions.

Cloudflare is changing how it grows and how it measures growth and Revenue and Consumption is becoming a core Go-To-Market (GTM) metric that shapes our GTM motions.

Working closely with GTM leaders and the Developer leadership team, we help define the metric, draft and enforce the Rules of Engagement (ROE) for Consumption, build the analytics and field reporting, and support enablement, landing, and continuous improvement. We are a partnering team and aim to work cross functionally to support our internal functions successfully in a consumption business. This is a new team, so you will be building the way we work, and we expect successful candidates to use AI every day to take on more than a team this size normally could.
About the Role
You will turn the Consumption strategy into working models, trusted data, and clear answers for the field. You will design, build, and land the targeting models, build scorecards with our cross-functional partners and Data and Analytics Leader, give Geo Ops analytics they need to run their business, and be the first stop when our field teams seek clarity on our data, reporting, and use this to improve our models.

Design, model, and land targets: Build and evolve our target setting model, and own the methodology. Back-test them, land them with GTM leaders, and keep improving them.

Build scorecards: Work with our DIA and GTM Analytics teams to build and maintain scorecards with cross-functional partners covering field performance, data quality, and disputes.
Protect data integrity: Validate actuals, baselines, targets, revenue attribution, and account ownership against source systems such as BigQuery, and tie GTM Revenue back to Finance and Billing.
Support the field and apply the Rules of Engagement: Answer field questions and cases on baselines, quotas, crediting, and ownership, applying the Rules of Engagement consistently and keeping a record of each decision. Spot where a rule needs to change, and provide the account hierarchy and ownership data teams need to collaborate across geos on our most critical customers.
Support territory planning and partner across teams: Provide analytics to Geo Ops and central territory design so they can deliver successful territory and coverage plans with equitable distribution of opportunity and targets. Work with Finance, Billing, data engineering, IT, RevOps, and Compensation to define data needs and move manual spreadsheet work into governed data products.
Use AI to scale the work: Use AI tools, to write and review SQL, speed up reconciliations, draft answers to common field questions, and automate recurring checks. Review every result for accuracy and follow Cloudflare policy on confidential data.

Experience: 5 or more years in sales operations, revenue operations, business analytics, target setting or territory modelling, or data operations, ideally in a usage-based or billing-driven business

SQL and data: Strong SQL on large datasets (BigQuery or similar), reconciling against CRM and billing data
Reporting: You have built scorecards or dashboards that other teams rely on
Controls and policy mindset: You understand why accuracy, documentation, and an audit trail matter when numbers drive pay, and you can apply a written policy such as the Rules of Engagement consistently to real cases

Salesforce: Experience with reports, SQL, account hierarchies, and ownership rules

About AI Gateway
AI inference is becoming core infrastructure. Every serious application will need access to many models across many providers, with reliability, observability, security, cost control, and routing built in from the start. AI Gateway is Cloudflare's bet that this layer belongs at the network edge: close to users, close to compute, and simple enough that a developer can adopt it with one API change.
Developers using AI Gateway need answers to two questions. Is the model I'm calling working the way you say it does? And which model should I be using at all? You'll lead the models team that answers both.
You'll start with model operations. That's the work behind every model in the catalog: provider integrations, capability testing, pricing and metering, capacity, security reviews, docs, health, and deprecations. Sometimes a launch needs to go live within minutes of a lab's announcement. Sometimes the right call is to hold it. Cloudflare is an infrastructure company at heart, so reliability and accuracy come first; speed comes from preparation and automation.
Then you'll bring model intelligence online. That means turning what we learn from Gateway traffic into decisions for customers: capability maps, per-task rankings, auto-routing profiles that pick the right model for each request, evals and regression detection, and market intelligence developers can trust.
This is a people-management role reporting to the AI Gateway Engineering Manager. You'll hire, develop, and lead the team, and you'll stay hands-on: writing code, building agent-driven workflows, and getting into the details of a failed launch or a suspicious eval SLO. Expect to manage people, projects, model stock, and operations all at once.
About the Role
Build and lead the models team: Hire, coach, and grow the people who run the catalog today and build its intelligence over time. Give people real ownership, give direct feedback, and grow leads who can run their own areas.
Run model launches end-to-end: Scope integrations, coordinate testing and evals, confirm pricing, metering, capacity, and security, and get docs and announcements ready. Prepare day-zero launches in advance so they can ship in minutes.
Keep the catalog true: Make sure what we publish (capabilities, limits, versions, prices) matches what developers actually get. Catch silent regressions, such as broken tool calling, truncated streams, quantization changes, or usage and pricing mismatches, before customers do.
Build model intelligence: As it comes online, own the evals, capability maps, and per-task rankings behind our auto-routing profiles and model recommendations. Make sure they measure what they claim to, and connect regressions to routing decisions so customers who chose "auto" aren't the ones who discover a problem.
Treat the catalog and intelligence as products: Have a point of view on which models belong in the catalog, which routing profiles to ship, and what market intelligence to publish. Base it on usage, quality, reliability, and cost data. Turn what you learn into roadmap input.
Run a lightweight operating cadence: Keep one source of truth for what's in flight, who owns it, what's blocked, and what ships next. Keep Engineering, Product, Partnerships, and other stakeholders aligned and informed without status meetings.
Automate relentlessly: Turn repeatable steps into scripts, tools, and agent workflows: endpoint validation, eval runs, catalog and pricing reconciliation, regression detection, and provider follow-ups. Manual effort per launch should fall as the catalog grows.
Responsibilities
Day-Zero & Quality Launches: Ensure new models launch on day zero with tested capabilities, accurate pricing, docs, and a clear call on routing eligibility.
Catalog Reliability & Health: Ensure the catalog reflects reality, and proactively identify when a model or provider is underperforming before customers notice.
Auto-Routing & Optimization: Deliver auto-routing that measurably beats a fixed model choice on cost or quality for users.
Developer Trust & Methodology: Build and maintain trusted rankings and recommendations grounded in solid methodology.
Partner & Stakeholder Management: Set clear expectations for providers, while keeping Engineering, Product, Partnerships, and other stakeholders aligned.
Team Leadership & Growth: Provide clear ownership and direction so the team knows what's next, who owns it, and how to grow into bigger roles.
Operational Scalability: Continually drive down the human effort required for each launch, eval, and routing update through tools and automation.
Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience
People Leadership: Experience hiring, managing, and growing engineers or operators, giving direct feedback, delegating real ownership, and expanding scope without becoming a bottleneck.
Technical & Shipping Capabilities: Proven track record of taking technical launches or integrations from ambiguity to production across teams and partners. Hands-on ability to write TypeScript, Python, or Rust, read API docs, inspect endpoints, and debug using terminal tools (logs, cURL).
Model Ecosystem Expertise: Deep familiarity with new models, labs, and inference providers. Hands-on understanding of streaming, tool calling, structured outputs, rate limits, token pricing, and provider-specific model behavior variations.
Product & SRE Mindset: Data-driven product instincts to advocate for adding, modifying, or retiring catalog items. SRE approach to defining, measuring, and alerting on service health, managing incidents calmly, and fixing root causes.
Agent Workflows & Detail-Oriented Execution: Daily experience building with agents—scoping work, verifying outputs, and integrating deterministic checks or human judgment appropriately. Meticulous attention to detail regarding model IDs, context limits, per-token prices, and response fields.
Bonus Qualifications (Nice to Have):
Experience at an inference provider, model lab, model router, eval platform, or API company.
Background in evals, ranking/recommendation systems, observability, metering, or usage-based billing.
Familiarity with Cloudflare Workers, AI Gateway, Workers AI, or Replicate.
Relevant domain backgrounds in engineering management, SRE, partner engineering, evals/applied ML, technical program management, or solutions engineering.

About the Department
Cloudflare’s engineering teams build and maintain the systems and products that power our global platform. A global platform which is within approximately 50 milliseconds of about 95% of the Internet connected population, serving on average, over 46 million HTTP requests per second.
About the Team
Delivering this platform with high performance and efficiency depends on advanced Linux kernel and hardware capabilities, and that is where this team works.
The Performance Team owns overall system and application performance across that fleet: resource optimization, instrumentation, and the tooling that lets us see what the hardware is actually doing. System memory sits alongside CPU cycles, network processing, and storage IOPS as a first-class resource, and how the kernel manages it is increasingly the thing that decides how hot we can safely run every machine we own.
We work upstream first. Several of us maintain or regularly contribute to the Linux kernel, and our default is to fix problems in mainline rather than carry private patches. This role is built on that principle.
The problem you would own
Using memory efficiently is one of the highest-leverage problems we have. At our scale, how the kernel's memory-management subsystem behaves under pressure has direct consequences for both performance and cost. As DRAM prices climb, getting more out of the memory we already own is a real lever on infrastructure spend.
Using custom low-overhead instrumentation on production servers, we have identified several scalability bottlenecks in the kernel memory layer that show up under real workloads. We are looking for an expert to take on these problems, fix them against production workloads, and drive the changes upstream. Solving them lifts efficiency and latency across the entire fleet rather than in one place.
What you will do
Diagnose and fix performance and scalability bottlenecks in the Linux kernel memory-management subsystem, informed by real production telemetry at a scale few environments can offer.
Land your work upstream. We expect MM changes to go to mainline first and want you to keep doing the maintainership and review work that earns standing in the community.
Build and extend low-overhead kernel instrumentation (tracepoints, BPF, perf) so we keep measuring before we change, and prove the impact afterwards.
Partner with kernel, networking, storage, and product engineers across the company to turn observed system behavior into concrete MM improvements.
Set technical direction for how Cloudflare uses, tunes, and evolves kernel memory management as we push utilization higher.
Requirements
Deep expertise in the Linux kernel memory-management subsystem: the page allocator, virtual memory and memory mapping, reclaim, and the locking and concurrency that hold it together.
A track record of upstream Linux contribution, ideally including maintainership or sustained work in MM or an adjacent subsystem.
Strong systems programming in C, with the judgement to make high-risk changes to shared infrastructure safely.
Ability to dive deep into a complex codebase while keeping the fleet-wide picture in mind, and to own a problem and its outcome rather than a single patch.
Clear communication with engineers across many teams, since the symptoms of an MM problem usually show up far from the MM code.
Bonuses

Experience troubleshooting and resolving performance issues in large-scale distributed systems.
Experience with large scale configuration/deployment management.

We're hiring a Principal for GTM Automation to document processes, build the AI agents and automation, and design improvements for our Revenue organization (Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Partner, RevOps). This is a senior individual contributor role where you will build and maintain the automation needed to drive efficiency and reduce operational friction.
The hard part of this job is knowing where not to put an agent. You'll decide which parts of prospecting, account research, deal management, and renewals can be handed to AI systems, where a person has to stay involved, and how we confirm the output is right before a seller acts on it. You will work directly with Sales leadership, Revenue Operations, Enablement, and the data and engineering teams on tools that save sellers real time. Success is identified by creating systems that resolve mundane tasks and save people real time. We are looking for someone who has run agentic systems in production for a business team and can tell us what broke and what they changed.

Design and build agentic workflows for repetitive revenue work such as account creation and enrichment, CRM updates, renewals, QBR prep, deal registration, account ownership, etc. Add RBAC, observability, error handling, etc. to make the systems as robust as possible.
Decide where AI and automation fit in the go-to-market motion, and where human judgment is still required.
Set the quality bar for agents in production: evals that run before every release, monitoring tied to pipeline and revenue, clear rules for sensitive data, and a tested rollback.
Own the architecture that connects agents to Salesforce, the data warehouse, enrichment and intent sources, and call data, so the next workflow reuses what the last one built.
Build the signal layer that feeds account prioritization, routing, and next-best-action. Product usage, intent, firmographic changes, and call transcripts all go in.
Review code and designs from stakeholders (analysts, Revenue Operations partners, etc.). Where version control, tests, or code review are missing, help put them in place.
Work with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success leaders to find the work worth automating, and say no to the work that isn't. Measure adoption and business impact for everything that ships. Retire tools that the organization isn’t using.
Track new models, agent frameworks, and vendor tools, and decide what's worth adopting.
Document each system and who owns it, so it keeps running when you move on to the next one.

10+ years in software engineering, data engineering, GTM automation, or revenue systems, with several years owning systems from design through production support at staff level or above.
At least one LLM-powered workflow or agent that a business team relied on in production. Be ready to walk us through how it called tools, handled failures, and was evaluated.
Strong Python or TypeScript, and strong SQL. You write tested code, and you can review AI-generated code well enough to catch what it gets wrong.
Hands-on Salesforce experience with the data model, Flow, APIs, and permissions, and a clear sense of how CRM data goes bad when automation writes to it. Comfort working directly in BigQuery, Snowflake, or a similar warehouse.
Experience integrating SaaS systems over REST APIs and webhooks, and tracing a failure back to its source.
Working knowledge of enrichment and signal tools such as D&B, ZoomInfo, and HG Insights, and a view on what to do when two sources disagree.
You can explain the same system to a sales VP in two sentences and to an engineer in a schema, and you can influence leaders on teams that don't report to you.

Establish and communicate technical strategy across multiple teams, translating long-term direction into incremental delivery plans.
Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives from problem definition through architecture, implementation, deployment, and operation.

Determine when AI is appropriate and when deterministic software offers a safer, simpler, or more reliable solution.

This position has working hours Monday to Friday, 09:00–18:00. Occasionally we support customers over weekends for specific changes that must be done outside their business hours. Travel is expected around 30%. Work is performed in English; fluency in Spanish or Portuguese is a strong advantage.

Plan and deliver timely and organized services for customers, ensure customers see the full value in Cloudflare’s products and advice on product best practices.
Gather business and technical requirements, use cases and any other information required to build, migrate and deliver a solution on behalf of the customer and transition the Cloudflare working environment to the customer. Produce a Solution Design, HLD, LLD, databuilds, procedures, scripts, test plans, drawings, deployment plan, migration plan, as-builts, and any other artifacts necessary to deliver the solution and transition smoothly into the customer’s technical teams.
Implement changes on behalf of the customer in the Cloudflare environment following the customer's change-management process. Provide guidance to the customer to configure their CPEs and integration points (identity providers, endpoints/MDM, DNS, network on-ramps, SIEM).
Troubleshoot implementation issues and collaborate with Customer Support, Engineering, and other teams to drive technical escalations to resolution.
Contribute to the success of the organization through knowledge-sharing — internal and external documentation, technical Q&A, and iterating on best practices. Build operational assets such as templates, automation scripts, procedures, and workflows.
Lead multi-workstream engagements and act as the senior technical owner for complex deployments; support pre-sales scoping and solution design; and mentor junior consultants, helping scale the practice through reusable intellectual property.
Experience might include a combination of the skills below:
3+ years in a customer-facing technical implementation or onboarding team, security engineering team, security operations center, or other highly technical team, including 3+ years focused on Zero Trust / SASE.
Strong command of the OSI model and core protocols: TCP/IP, TLS (including TLSv1.3 and mTLS), DNS, HTTP/2.
Deep understanding of Zero Trust technologies: Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), Secure Web Gateway (SWG), Remote Browser Isolation (RBI), Data Loss Prevention (DLP), CASB, and Cloud Email Security.
Deep understanding of internet and security technologies: forward and reverse proxies with content filtering & DLP, sandboxing, firewalls/NGFW, WAF, bot management, rate limiting, and SSL/IPsec & SSL/TLS VPN appliances and services.
Modern identity: SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM user/group provisioning and deprovisioning, LDAP/Active Directory, MFA/FIDO2, and the role of the IdP — with hands-on experience on Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, or Ping.
DNS in depth: DNS filtering, DoH/DoT, conditional forwarding / split-DNS, internal-zone resolution, and local domain fallback.
Endpoints: software distribution and deployment across Windows, macOS, and Linux; Windows and Linux server administration; and client-endpoint troubleshooting across all three platforms.
Networking troubleshooting: debugging network connectivity with standard tools (packet capture, DNS/HTTP tracing).
Ability to manage a project, work to deadlines, and prioritize between competing demands.
Work performed in English; fluency in Spanish or Portuguese is a strong advantage.
Demonstrated technical experience (hands-on-keyboard) with:
At the senior level we expect these to be hands-on-keyboard — configured, deployed, migrated, or troubleshot in production — not just understood conceptually.
Experience working with Reverse & Forward proxies with Content Filtering & DLP technologies
Software distribution & deployment in Microsoft, Mac and Linux environments
Detailed working knowledge of web based security, network segmentation, security proxies, Firewalls and NGFWs, SSL/IPSec and SSL/TLS VPN appliances & services, etc
Integrating identity providers with enterprise applications end to end — SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM provisioning, group/attribute mapping, and troubleshooting the IdP handshake.
Windows & Linux Server system administration
Windows, MacOS and Linux client endpoints troubleshooting
Experience debugging Network connectivity issues using Network Troubleshooting Tools
Preferred but not mandatory:
Automation / Infrastructure-as-Code: Terraform (ideally the Cloudflare provider), REST APIs, Python/Bash scripting, Git, CI/CD, and policy-as-code.
Cloud platforms: AWS / Azure / GCP networking — VPC/VNet, Security Groups / NSG / NACL, cloud-native DNS resolvers (Route 53 Inbound Endpoints, Azure Private DNS), cloud IAM, and deploying connectors in IaaS.
SASE on-ramp networking: IPsec/GRE tunnel configuration, BGP, Anycast, network segmentation for Zero Trust, and SD-WAN / MPLS / WAN-optimization background.
MDM software distribution (Intune, Jamf).
Identity & directory tooling: Microsoft Active Directory, GPO, Entra ID, and Intune.
Observability: log export (Logpush) and SIEM integration (Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Elastic, Chronicle); Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX).
Frameworks & compliance: NIST Zero Trust Architecture; GDPR, DORA, NIS2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOC 2 (FedRAMP if US-government work applies).
Certifications: CISSP, CCSP, SC-300, AZ-500, AWS Security Specialty, CCNP/CCIE, CompTIA, or equivalent are a strong plus. Forensic certifications (GCFA, GCFE, GCIA, GCIH) are welcome but not central to this role.
Emerging: familiarity with AI security / shadow-AI governance — AI-tool discovery and gating, and AI Gateway concepts.

Cloudflare is building a new public Certificate Authority for the Internet. We are looking for a senior technical architect to help define the systems, protocols, and security architecture behind it.
This role spans applied cryptography, Web PKI, distributed systems, security engineering, compliance, and Internet standards. It will help Cloudflare build a CA that operates safely at Internet scale while establishing a credible path from today's X.509 ecosystem toward post-quantum authentication using Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs).
Mission
Define and guide the end-to-end architecture of Cloudflare's public Certificate Authority: a high-assurance, highly available system capable of issuing conventional publicly trusted certificates at Cloudflare scale while supporting Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs) and the evolution toward a post-quantum Web PKI.
You will help determine not only how the CA is implemented, but also its trust boundaries, key hierarchy, issuance architecture, auditability, failure modes, incident response mechanisms, and long-term cryptographic evolution.
Key Responsibilities
Define and maintain the end-to-end technical architecture of Cloudflare's public CA across certificate issuance, key management, transparency, revocation, renewal, and relying-party integration.
Design root and intermediate CA trust hierarchies, signing systems, HSM integration, key ceremonies, key rotation, backup, recovery, migration, and key-compromise response.
Architect secure, resilient, and highly available issuance services capable of operating at Internet scale and across multiple geographic and failure domains.
Design certificate lifecycle systems around ACME, domain and IP validation, CAA, Certificate Transparency, pre-issuance linting, revocation, renewal, and large-scale certificate replacement.
Integrate Cloudflare’s MTC infrastructure, including CA logs, landmarks,, cosigning or mirroring, and interactions with relying parties.
Develop practical architectures for coexistence and migration between classical X.509 certificates and post-quantum authentication mechanisms.
Define trust boundaries, security properties, and threat models covering key compromise, unauthorized issuance, software supply-chain compromise, operator error, malicious insiders, infrastructure failure, split views, and cryptographic migration.
Design systems that make CA behavior observable and independently verifiable through transparency mechanisms, reproducible builds, cryptographic attestations, public operational telemetry, tamper-evident evidence, and audit controls.
Design failure containment and recovery mechanisms that support safe certificate replacement, revocation, key rotation, and incident response without creating avoidable Internet availability failures.
Translate CA/Browser Forum requirements, browser and operating-system root-program policies, audit criteria, and certification requirements into concrete technical and operational controls.
Review protocols, architecture, and implementations with an adversarial mindset, identifying assumptions and failure modes that do not hold at Internet scale.
Work closely with Cloudflare's cryptography, TLS, security, networking, infrastructure, compliance, product, and operations teams.
Provide architectural direction, design review, and technical mentorship to engineers implementing and operating the CA platform.
Represent Cloudflare in relevant standards and industry work, collaborating with browser vendors, root programs, researchers, auditors, CA operators, and the wider Web PKI community.
What You'll Bring
Substantial experience designing or operating security-critical systems, with deep expertise in at least one of: public Certificate Authorities, Web PKI, applied cryptography, TLS and Internet security protocols, Certificate Transparency, hardware-backed key management, or large-scale distributed security systems.
Strong knowledge of certificate trust chains, issuance and validation, revocation, key lifecycle management, and the security and availability implications of CA design decisions.
Experience defining system trust boundaries, threat models, security invariants, and failure-handling strategies.
Ability to reason about systems in which a subtle architectural or operational mistake can affect a significant fraction of the Internet.
Experience leading architecture across multiple engineering teams without relying solely on organizational authority.
Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain cryptographic and architectural tradeoffs to engineers, auditors, standards participants, and senior stakeholders.
Comfort operating with substantial autonomy in an evolving technical and policy environment.

About the Role
Digital Native SEs at Cloudflare work with the most innovative and cutting-edge companies on the planet — the startups and high-growth, cloud-native businesses that are building the next generation of Internet products. These are companies where the developers are the decision makers, and where the CTO is often personally responsible for shipping new products and getting the company's AI initiatives off the ground.
This role is for a technologist who genuinely enjoys being in the room with builders. You'll be equally comfortable jumping into a Slack channel with a founding engineer, whiteboarding an architecture with a lead developer, and stepping into a strategic conversation with a CTO about their platform and AI roadmap. You speak the language of engineers fluently and can hold a credible, detailed technical conversation — but this is not a software developer role, and you won't be writing production code every day. Your superpower is technical discovery, translation, and evangelism: understanding what a builder is trying to accomplish, mapping it to the full breadth of the Cloudflare Developer Platform, and inspiring teams to build on Cloudflare rather than just consume a single service.
The Digital Native segment leans heavily on Solutions Engineering to lead technical discovery within the cloud-developer vertical. You'll be expected to go deep on the Cloudflare Developer Platform — Workers, Durable Objects, Workers AI, R2, KV, D1, Vectorize, Queues, Pages, and the broader developer ecosystem — far beyond basic storage, and to make the case for Cloudflare as the place to build. This role covers both the acquisition of new Digital Native accounts and the expansion of existing ones. Technical Validation: Partner closely with Account Executives to lead technical deep-dive discovery, capture business requirements, and map complex customer infrastructure - DNS, CDN, Zero Trust, Network Security, Workers - to fit-for-purpose Cloudflare architectures and bespoke solutions. . Deliver tailored technical presentations, architectural diagrams, and demonstrations that show how Cloudflare solves specific performance, security, and reliability challenges. Experience: Experience in a customer-facing technical role, such as Solutions Engineering, Customer Engineering, Professional Services, Sales Engineering, Technical Account Management, or as a Forward Deployed Engineer (years of experience required will vary based on Associate, Senior, Staff, or Principal leveling).

Internet fundamentals: Deep understanding of how the Internet works, including OSI Model layers 1–7, BGP, GRE, TCP/UDP, DNS (authoritative and recursive), HTTP(S), and SSL/TLS.
Security: Expertise in the security of Internet properties, including WAF, Bot Management, Firewalls, Rate Limiting, (M)TLS, Zero Trust, and SASE concepts.
Performance: Expertise in the performance of Internet properties, including speed, latency, caching, video streaming, HTTP/2, and TLS 1.3.

Hyperscaler / Digital Native Background: Talent coming out of hyperscalers, digital natives, distributed systems environments, or startups is strongly valued for its deeper cloud fluency and advanced architecture depth.
Education
Undergraduate or graduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
Travel
This role may require travel up to 20–50% to attend customer meetings, conferences, industry events, and in-person team collaboration.
Compensation
This role features a competitive base salary and a variable compensation structure tied directly to the successful execution of full-lifecycle commercial targets, including new business acquisition, ongoing adoption milestones, and overall account expansion. Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location.

This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan.

Dental Insurance

On-demand mental health support and Employee Assistance Program
Global Travel Medical Insurance

401(k) Retirement Savings Plan
Employee Stock Participation Plan

Leave programs, including parental, pregnancy health, medical, and bereavement leave

Project Galileo : Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.
Athenian Project : In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.
1.1.1.1 : We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. About Us
At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.
At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.
Available Location: New York, US
